stem: In the context of respiratory distress in infants, what is the physiological purpose of 'grunting'?

options.text: To increase end-expiratory pressure and splint the lungs open.
To clear mucus from the upper airway passages.
To decrease the heart rate during periods of stress.
To facilitate the closure of the foramen ovale.

explanation: By closing the glottis during expiration, the infant creates 'auto-PEEP,' which helps keep the stiff, fluid-filled lungs inflated.
rationale: The lecturer compares this behavior to an artificial setting used in the Intensive Care Unit.

optionExplanations.A: By closing the glottis during expiration, the infant creates 'auto-PEEP,' which helps keep the stiff, fluid-filled lungs inflated.
optionExplanations.B: Grunting is a sign of alveolar distress or lung stiffness rather than a mechanism for clearing secretions.
optionExplanations.C: Grunting is part of the work of breathing and is actually associated with a high-stress, high-catecholamine state.
optionExplanations.D: The closure of the foramen ovale is dependent on atrial pressure changes at birth, not the expiratory grunting mechanism.

source.hint: The lecturer compares this behavior to an artificial setting used in the Intensive Care Unit.
